commitResults.messageTitle: Add Level-1: Echo user commands until bye
Add Level-2: Store and list items
commitResults.messageBody:
Replace the echo behaviour with storage: any input that is not a known
command is kept in a fixed-size String[100] and confirmed with 'added: X',
and the 'list' command prints the collection numbered from 1. The brief
allows assuming at most 100 items, so a fixed array plus an item count is
sufficient and avoids introducing collections before the course covers them.

Pass the array and count as method parameters rather than making them static
fields, so each print method declares what it depends on. Guard the 101st
item with an in-character message instead of letting the array index throw.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Level-3: Mark tasks as done, extract Task class
commitResults.messageBody:
Add 'mark <n>' and 'unmark <n>' so the user can track which tasks are
finished, and show each task's status as [X] or [ ] in the list.

Extract a Task class into its own file (A-Classes) to hold the description
and done flag together, replacing the parallel String array. Fields are
protected rather than private so later increments can add specialised task
types that inherit from it. Task.toString() renders the status box so the
list and the mark/unmark confirmations share one format.

Guard against a missing, non-numeric, or out-of-range task number so a
mistyped command reports the problem instead of throwing.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add A-CodingStandard: Adopt the SE-EDU Java coding standard
commitResults.messageBody:
Review the code against the intermediate-level SE-EDU Java coding standard
and fix two violations: rename the command constants so related constants
share a common prefix (COMMAND_MARK, COMMAND_UNMARK) as the grouping rule
requires, and replace the unexplained two-space literal in
printStatusChanged with the named INDENT_DETAIL constant.

Record the standard in AGENTS.md so it binds all future code rather than
being a one-off cleanup, along with the points that recur in this project.
Document the default-package deviation as deliberate: the standard requires
every class to belong to a package, but the course introduces packages in
the later A-Packages increment.

No behaviour change; the Level-3 scenarios produce identical output.
